A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EUBRL research and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–K. Text, equations, tables, and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original EUBRL experiments on Chain, Loop, DeepSea, and LazyChain, including results in Tables 1 and 3 and Figures 1–3.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Section 5, Tables 1 and 3, and Figures 1–3.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the epistemically guided reward, posterior updates, and planning procedures are unchanged. The model specifications and uncertainty formulations in Appendix B are also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Chain, Loop, DeepSea, and LazyChain with the same deterministic/stochastic variants and problem-size coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches within Tables 1 and 3 and Figures 1–3. The newly mentioned Langevin Monte Carlo methods in Appendix B.3 are examples of possible uncertainty estimators, without reported baseline evaluations.

E3.justification: The 1,000-step Chain/Loop evaluations, task-completion criteria, DeepSea/LazyChain step limits, hyperparameter searches, and discount factors remain unchanged in Section 5 and Appendix C.1–C.3.

E4.justification: The existing scaling analyses, conservative/exploratory prior comparison, tied-prior variant, and variance-versus-mutual-information comparison are retained. No ablations, robustness tests, or supplementary empirical analyses are added or removed.

E5.justification: Both retain standard-error reporting in Tables 1 and 3, 500-seed evaluations in those tables and Figure 1, and 20-seed evaluations in Figures 2–3. Uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical entries, plotted results, and reported findings match. For example, EUBRL retains average return 3473 with SE 16 on Chain and 395 with SE 0.04 on Loop. The experimental figure images are identical.

T1.justification: The regret and sample-complexity bounds, prior assumptions, counterexamples, and proofs in Section 4 and Appendices D–K are unchanged. Equation reflow and spacing adjustments do not change mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about epistemic guidance, nearly minimax-optimal guarantees for the specified prior class, and superior sample efficiency, scalability, and consistency.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the experimental advantages, prior-misspecification warnings, and limitations concerning function approximation remain unchanged. The added Langevin example does not revise Appendix B.3's scalability argument.

D1.justification: New Appendix C.4 identifies the EUBRL code repository, states its GPLv3 license, and documents its derivation from bayesrl and baseline-alignment efforts. This adds access and provenance information; existing implementation settings and hyperparameters are unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix B.3 adds Langevin Monte Carlo as an approximate Bayesian estimation approach, citing Welling and Teh (2011) and Ishfaq et al. (2024). These two references modestly extend literature coverage without changing the broader research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds funding acknowledgments and Appendix C.4, briefly expands Appendix B.3, and corrects 'tigher' to 'tighter' in Appendix G.7.2. The main narrative and existing section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds an ICLR 2026 running header and introduces limited reference and appendix reflow, including repositioning Table 4 at the top of page 21. Figure content, table structures, and captions remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Appendix C.4 improves reproducibility documentation by supplying code-location, license, and implementation-provenance information absent from v1. The two added citations also modestly improve literature coverage. These are limited gains, with the scientific evidence, theoretical support, and substantive limitations unchanged.
